notes:
Summary: Closed-lost to hyperscaler managed endpoints (AWS SageMaker). Team liked Redwood performance and the Optimize recommendations, but final decision driven by procurement friction and security preferences.

Call notes / CRM fragments:
- 9/18: AE Evan intro — "fast ROI for chat we need"; asked for cost model and dedicated vs hosted analysis. Shared deck.
- 10/02 demo: SE Priya ran 2 live routes (chat + rerank). Latency 95th=220ms in dedicated POC — team happy.
- 11/13 security review: SecOps insisted on native CloudTrail logs, AWS KMS key policies and centralized SIEM integration. They viewed these as "must-have" for procurement (quote: "we can't add another vendor that changes our audit pipeline").
- POC feedback: performance comparable, but Redwood required extra steps to wire private KMS and custom audit forwarding into their SOC stack; they estimated ~4-6w of infra work vs near-zero for managed endpoints.
- Procurement notes: NorthStar has existing cloud committed spend and preferred to consolidate under AWS to preserve discounts and simplify billing. Also leadership issued a hiring/budget freeze for new vendors Jan-Mar which lowered willingness to onboard a new vendor.
- Internal champion risk: ML platform lead (Samuel Ortiz) left Dec 2025; no clear replacement to drive cross-org integration.

What we pitched: Dedicated + Private (VPC) with KMS integrations and audit hooks; Redwood Optimize to reduce unit cost; rollout plan with canary and automatic fallback. They liked the features but judged integration/time-to-production as higher risk than a native cloud endpoint.

Next actions taken:
- 1/10: AE marked closed-lost. Sent W/L request. Follow-up planned: 6-month nurture (quarterly check-ins), offer a short integration guide for cloud-native KMS handshake if they revisit.

Useful links / artifacts: drive/NSYS_Redwood_eval_deck_v2.pptx, drive/northstar-security-faq.pdf, gmail_thread_1752948 (pricing negotiation thread), AIINF-1129 (POC infra question).
